obligation: Internal report of a suspected incident or suspect product
trigger: Any workforce member in any division notices a suspected incident, including suspect or tampered products
deadline: Within 1 hour of noticing it
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all divisions
notifying_entity: Reporting division (here Logistics receiving and the IC-2 team)
clock_starts: Time the workforce member noticed it

obligation: DFARS cyber incident report affecting covered defense information
trigger: Discovery of a cyber incident that affects a covered contractor information system or the covered defense information in it (here: a tampered switch powered on in the IC-2 lab network where CUI configuration templates were loaded)
deadline: Within 72 hours of discovery ("rapidly report" as defined in 252.204-7012(a))
notify: DoD through DIBNet (requires a DoD-approved medium assurance certificate)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - triggered in this scenario
clock_starts: Discovery of the cyber incident by the SOC (Day 0)

obligation: Incident report number to the prime
trigger: Federal Solutions submits a DIBNet report on a subcontract
deadline: As soon as practicable after the DIBNet report
notify: Prime D (next higher-tier contractor); also Primes whose jobs used affected units
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Prime D integration jobs

obligation: Malicious software submission and media preservation
trigger: Malicious software isolated, or any cyber incident reported under 252.204-7012(c)
deadline: Submit malware as DoD instructs; preserve images and monitoring data for at least 90 days from the report
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the firmware implant and lab images

obligation: Covered telecommunications or video surveillance equipment identified
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) (Section 889); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Identification of covered telecommunications or video surveillance equipment or services used as a substantial or essential component of any system during contract performance
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; further information within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: Contracting officer (DoD: through DIBNet); tell the prime the same day
applies_at_this_tier: Evaluate - not triggered in this scenario because the affected products are from a manufacturer that is not covered (checked Day 1); stays on the checklist for every product incident

citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Identification of a covered article (Kaspersky hardware, software, or services) during contract performance, where the contract includes the clause
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further information within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: Evaluate - only where the clause is in the contract; not triggered in this scenario

citation: FAR 52.204-30; FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Identification of a covered article subject to a FASCSA order, where the contract includes the clause
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further information within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: Evaluate - only where the clause is in the contract; not triggered in this scenario

obligation: Electronic parts that cannot be confirmed as new and unused or came from outside the sourcing order
trigger: An electronic part for a DoD job came from a source other than the original manufacturer, its authorized suppliers, or a contractor-approved supplier, or cannot be confirmed as new and unused
deadline: Promptly, in writing; keep inspection, testing, and authentication records
applies_at_this_tier: Evaluate - Supplier K is an authorized supplier, but the 96 switches allocated to integration jobs can no longer be confirmed as unaltered; counsel decided on Day 2 to notify
clock_starts: Determination that parts cannot be confirmed

citation: Reseller agreements (contract); FTC Act Section 5 (no deceptive omissions)
trigger: Resellers received affected serials
deadline: As the reseller agreements require; target within 2 business days of confirming affected serials
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual
clock_starts: Confirmation of the affected serial list

citation: Voluntary; FTC Act Section 5 (15 U.S.C. 45(a)) informs content
trigger: Consumers bought affected routers
deadline: As soon as a safe remediation (firmware restore or replacement) is ready; counsel approves content
notify: About 2,900 consumers in 41 states (email, app, and order history)

deadline: Within 72 hours of confirming the client is affected (contract term)

obligation: Card brand compromise reporting: Visa worked example (contractual)
citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0 (effective 2026-06-25), Sections A.1-A.3 and A.5; Visa Core Rules 10.3.1.2. Card brand rules applied through the acquiring bank, not law. If the business accepts American Express, the DSOP (April 2026, Section 3) requires notice to American Express within 72 hours of discovery. Mastercard and Discover rules not verified
trigger: Evidence sufficient to raise a reasonable suspicion of, or to confirm, unauthorized access to Visa account data or a system that stores, processes or transmits it
deadline: Tell the acquiring bank immediately (A.3.1). Make sure the event is reported to Visa within 3 calendar days of the suspicion or confirmation (A.1.1), then send the incident report within 3 calendar days of that notice (A.2.1). If Visa requires a PCI Forensic Investigator, retain one within 5 business days (A.5.1.1)
notify: Acquiring bank; Visa Global Risk Investigations, through the acquiring bank. Other brands as the acquiring bank directs
applies_at_this_tier: No - no cardholder data involved in this scenario
clock_starts: Suspicion of an account data compromise

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information held by the group (definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example "without unreasonable delay" or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where required; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Evaluate - not triggered unless analysis finds group-held personal information was accessed (for example through Supplier K access to the supplier portal); apply each state where affected individuals reside
clock_starts: Determination of a breach under each state law

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach (a 15-day extension is possible for good cause, for this notice to individuals only)
applies_at_this_tier: Evaluate - as above

applies_at_this_tier: Evaluate - if 500 or more Florida residents

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at one time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
applies_at_this_tier: Evaluate - if more than 1,000

trigger: Logistics, as a third-party agent holding 3PL clients consumer shipping data, has a breach of that data
